Hi Guillaume,

I tried to set up your model and got the following warning, which indicates there's an issue with the indexing for `theta` and `data_RR`.

I haven't looked to see how that would impact mixing, but best to fix that first and then see if there is still a problem.

-chris

Defining model

            `theta[i, j, t] <- phi((log(i - (i - j) + 0.5) - lambda[t, I_lambda_1[i, j, t]])/phi_[t]) - nimStep(i - (i - j)) * phi((log(i - (i - j) - 0.5) - lambda[t, I_lambda_1[i, j, t]])/phi_[t])`?

On Thu, Mar 28, 2024 at 2:02 PM guillaum...@gmail.com <guillaum...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi everyone,

I am currently running into convergence issues and not too sure how to address this so hoping to get some feedback/pointers on how to proceed!


Context:

I am running a daily capture mark recapture model to estimate abundance of a fish run migrating from the river to the sea.

Each year a trap is operating (almost) daily, fish captured are marked and released a couple of km upstream and we record any recaptures.

Fish migration occur during a short period (a few weeks).

Ideally, we would like to run the trap have a couple of days with 0 captures a ramp up to a maximum and a ramp down followed by again a few 0.

The trick is that, the trap is not always operational during the whole migration and as a consequence some years the trap is installed and we get a bunch of fish from day 1.

To compensate for the potential missing part of the run , I am trying to estimate the probability of a fish to migrate based on temperature/ discharge and using it to obtain the proportion of fish migrating on a given day and therefore available to be captured by a trap when operational.

 It’s been a bit of a struggle to write the model because I had to line up the different time frame i.e. no matter if a trap is installed or not, fish are migrating within a 91 day window and then every year a trap is operational between 11 (!) and 45 days.

Sometimes the trap is not operational for a couple of days and therefore we are losing recapture opportunities. So there is a lot of indexing involved.

Anyway, I think I have things now written correctly. I can compile and run the model however the mixing is poor: I get high Rhats and very small effective sampling size, for a given parameter, some chains seem to get locked on different values.

 I have tried to generate a configuration from the autoblock function to improve things with little success.
when trying to build the MCMC object I get the following error message:
"nimble Cannot assign a joint sampler to simultaneously update both posterior predictive and non-posterior predictive nodes"

 

So I’m left wondering if my data is insufficient to estimate the various parameters/variables I am looking at or if it’s a sampling issue and if so, how to address it.

Love to hear any feedback about this! 

Attached Rdata with model, constants, Data and inits and script I am using to compile and run.

 

Thanks

 

Guillaume
